                                                               SECTION B

                      DEFINITIONS, GENERAL PRINCIPLES, RECOMMENDATIONS AND STANDARDS

20. PROCESSING AND HANDLING

20.1. General

General Principle

Organic processing and handling provide consumers with supplies of certified organic products, and organic
farmers with a market without compromise to the organic integrity of their products.

Requirements:

                                                        South African specific
 Producers are required to have documented policies and procedures ensuring that these requirements are kept.
 HACCP type protocols, including Organic Control Points, which ensure organic integrity, should be implemented
 as a minimum. Compliance with all national legislation is required.

20.1.1. Handlers and processors shall not co-mingle organic products with non-organic products.

20.1.2. Handlers and processers shall ensure traceability in the organic processing and handling chain.

20.1.3. All organic products shall be clearly identified / labelled as such and processed, stored and transported in
a way that prevents co-mingling, contamination and or substitution by or physical contact with non-certified
products.

20.1.4. When non-organic products are prepared or stored in the preparation unit, the operator shall inform the
control body.

20.1.5. The handler or processor shall take all necessary measures to prevent organic products from being
contaminated by pollutants and contaminants, including the cleaning, decontamination, or if necessary,
disinfection of facilities and equipment.

20.1.6. The handler or processor shall identify and minimize risks of environmental pollution resulting from
their activity.

20.1.7. Processors shall respect the principles of good manufacturing practices. This shall include maintaining
appropriate procedures based on identification of critical processing steps.

20.2. Ingredients

General Principle

Organic processed products are made from organic ingredients.

Requirements:

20.2.1. Ingredients of agricultural origin used in an organic processed product shall be organically produced in
accordance with the labelling requirements (Section 22 Labelling, clause 22.1.3.) except for those additives and
processing aids that appear in Appendix 4.

                                                    Regional or other exception
 In cases where an ingredient of organic origin is commercially unavailable in sufficient quality or quantity,
 operators may use non-organic raw materials, provided that:

                  Registration 082-929-NPO Email: info@saoso.org Tel: (010) 786 0398. Web: www.saoso.org

   a           They are not genetically engineered or contain nano-materials;

   b           The current lack of availability in that region is officially recognized or prior permission

               from the control body is obtained. Official recognition may be by inclusion on a government

               or certification body list of permitted non-organic agricultural ingredients;

   c           The requirements in Section 22 Labelling, clause 22.1.3. shall be met.

20.2.2. Using organic and non-organic forms of the same ingredient in a single product is prohibited.

20.2.3. Water and salt may be used as ingredients in the production of organic products and are not included in
the percentage calculations of organic ingredients.

20.2.4. Minerals (including trace elements) and vitamins shall not be used to fortify product unless their use is
legally required or where severe dietary or nutritional deficiency can be demonstrated in the market to which the
particular batch of product is destined.

20.2.5. Preparations of micro-organisms and enzymes commonly used in food processing may be used, with the
exception of genetically engineered micro- organisms and their products.

20.2.6. For the production of organic micro-organisms for processed food and feed, only organically produced
substrate shall be used.

20.3. Processing Methods

General Principle

Organic processing and handling provide the consumer with supplies of organic products without compromise to
the integrity of the products and protects the environment.

Requirements:

20.3.1. Techniques used to process organic products shall be biological, physical, and mechanical in nature. Any
additives, processing aids, or other material must be organically produced or appear in Appendix 4 Table 1 and
shall be used in accordance with noted restrictions.

                                         South African guidelines

The following processes may be used:

   a           Mechanical and physical;

   b           Biological;

   c           Smoking;

   d           Extraction;

   e           Precipitation;

   f           Filtration;

   g           Distillation;

   h           Microwaving.

20.3.2. Substances and techniques shall not be used that:

a              Reconstitute properties lost by the processing and storage of organic products;

b              Conceal negligent processing;

c              Or may otherwise be misleading as to the true nature of these products. Water may be used for

               re-hydration or reconstitution.

      Registration 082-929-NPO Email: info@saoso.org Tel: (010) 786 0398. Web: www.saoso.org
                           Postnet Suite 855 Private Bag X153 Houghton, 2021 Gauteng
                                  © The South African Organic Sector Organisation

                                                                                                                  P a g e | 61
20.3.3. Solvents used to extract organic products shall be either organically produced or food grade substances
that appear in Appendix 4, Table 1 consistent with the annotation.

20.3.4. Irradiation is not permitted for any ingredient or the final product.

20.3.5. Filtration equipment shall not contain asbestos or utilize techniques or substances that may contaminate
the product. Filtration agents and adjuvants are considered processing aids and therefore must appear in
Appendix 4.

20.3.6. The following conditions of storage are permitted (for allowed substances in these conditions, see
Appendix 4):

a              Controlled atmosphere;

b              Temperature control;

c              Drying;

d              Humidity regulation.

20.3.7. Intentional manufacture or use of manufactured nanomaterials in organic products is prohibited.

20.3.8. Equipment surfaces and utensils that might come into contact with organic products shall be free of
manufactured nanomaterials, unless there is verified absence of contamination risk.

20.4. Pest and Disease Control

General Principle

Organic products are protected from pests and diseases by the use of good manufacturing practices that include
proper cleaning, sanitation and hygiene, without the use of chemical pest control treatments or irradiation.

Requirements:

20.4.1. Handlers and processors shall manage pests and shall use the following methods according to these
priorities:

a              Preventative methods such as disruption, elimination of habitat and access to facilities;

b              Mechanical, physical and biological methods, including visual detection, sound, ultra-sound, light

               and UV-light, temperature control, controlled atmosphere and diatomaceous earth.

c              Substances according to the Appendices of this Standard;

d              Substances (other than pesticides) used in traps.

20.4.2. Prohibited pest control practices include, but are not limited to, the following substances and methods:

a              Pesticides not contained in Appendix 3;

b              Fumigation with ethylene oxide, methyl bromide, aluminium phosphide or other substance not

               contained in Appendix 4;

c              Ionizing radiation / irradiation / radurisation.

20.4.3. The direct use or application of a prohibited method or material renders that product no longer organic.
The operator shall take necessary precautions to prevent contamination, including the removal of organic
products and related packaging materials from the storage or processing facility, and measures to decontaminate
